entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text: The appellant is the accused in Crime No.125 of 2024 of Kunnicode Police Station.

The appellant allegedly had committed offences punishable under Section 376(1), 506 and 376(2)(n) of the Indian Penal Code, 1860 and under Sections 3(1)(w)(i), 3(1)(w)(ii) and 3(2)(v) of the SC/ST Act.
The Special Court, Kottarakkara dismissed his application for bail.

2. Heard the learned counsel for the appellant, the learned counsel for the de facto complainant and the learned Public Prosecutor.
3. The prosecution allegation is that the appellant on giving a false assurance to the de facto complainant that he would marry her, took her on 30.01.2023 to the house of one Aneesh and thereafter on 07.02.2023 to Malappuram.
On the way, they stayed in a lodge at Changanassery and the appellant subjected the de facto complainant to sexual intercourse there.
Later, they lived together for three months in the house of one Niyas, a relative of the appellant, as husband and wife.
During that period also she was subjected to sexual intercourse.
Subsequently the appellant retracted from the assurance and thereby he has committed the offence of rape.
He also threatened the de facto complainant that her nude photographs will be publicised in the social media.
4. The appellant would contend that he did not involve in the alleged crime and without any material or evidence, he has been implicated in the crime.
He is innocent.
The investigation in the matter has progressed considerably and there is no reason or justification for his further detention.

5. The learned Public Prosecutor submitted that considering the seriousness of the offence and the possibility of interfering with the investigation by the appellant in the event of his release on bail,
this appeal deserves only to be dismissed.
6. The appellant was arrested on 02.02.2024.
The investigation in the matter has progressed to a considerable extent.
The learned counsel for the de facto complainant expressed the anguish that there is every chance for the appellant to publicise her objectionable photographs in the event of his release on bail.
I am of the view that the said apprehension cannot be a reason to deny bail since the appellant has been in custody since 02.02.2024.
Having heard the learned counsel on either side and considering the nature and gravity of the offence, further detention of the appellant is unnecessary.
I am therefore of the view that the appellant is entitled to be released on bail.

7. In the result, the appeal is allowed and the appellant is granted bail on his executing a bond for Rs.50,000/- (Rupees fifty thousand only), with two solvent sureties for the like amount each, to the Shalu Sajeev vs State Of Kerala on 15 March, 2024
